trigger.snippet: Solution: Pi's storage is working state and stays local, SQLite in a clone and thrown away on a runner. Hosts share the record through core's `RecordStore` port: add a batch of immutable records, list a changeset's records, fresh or not at all, one compare-and-set cell per changeset for the publication lease, and dispose. The contract assumes no ordering, history, transaction, secrecy or writer identity, so git, a directory, an object store or a database can meet it, and every adapter runs one conformance suite. The git adapter keeps `melian/state`, commits built with git's plumbing and never a checkout, `--force-with-lease` with backoff, and a wall-clock deadline; a record is a plain JSON file, and one commit holds a batch. Every store refuses a record past core's `recordLimit`, 4 MiB, and the relay takes a file up to that limit and a batch up to twice it. A guardrails record that would pass the limit keeps every finding's ID, severity and place. It leaves out the detail of its last findings in ID order, as [issue #605](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/605) asked. Every other check's record gets the same budget, so Biome, tsc, Enola or mutation findings past it are trimmed alike. A record that cannot fit even so fails its check, and the review reads not reviewed, by the maintainer's ruling that [the decision](decisions/2026-11-20-guardrails-record-fits-the-store.md) records. It builds commits in a bare repository of its own beside the clone, `records.git`, and fetches the branch's whole history into it. A file Melian did not write refuses work on the changeset whose folder holds it, or all work when it sits anywhere else, by [the amending decision](decisions/2026-11-14-git-record-store-refuses-by-location.md). A record counts because the store accepted it, so the store's write access is the trust, and no writer holds a key; a repository with `trust.writers: false`, or one that takes pull requests from forks, pins the trusted host's one key, and a store that is no branch of the repository is trusted only when the base's policy writes that out. In CI, a job that ran a head's code hands its records to one that ran none, which adds only the kinds a review writes, so a head's code can never dismiss. A fork's head hands over only the results of checks that run its code, today `static.mutation` alone, and the job that holds the key writes the fork's account and round itself, as [the account record decision](decisions/2026-11-16-account-record.md) records. An account names the resolution policy its round was decided under by fingerprint, and a reader decides the round only under that policy: under another, or with none, or for an account that names none or predates the field, the round reads not reviewed, as [its amendment](decisions/2026-11-16-account-names-its-resolution-policy.md) records. A record written before Melian withheld outside text fails its payload check, so a store that holds one fails its checks until the record is removed, as [the later amendment](decisions/2026-11-18-records-before-withheld-text-are-refused.md) records. A result's key is the hash of the whole request its producer was given, so no key can leave out an input. Core's `KeyedRequest` builds that key, and triage, check runs, verification and walkthroughs use it, as [the request keys decision](decisions/2026-11-14-request-keys-as-built.md) records; the lens run follows. Another host resumes by building its own requests, importing the records whose keys match, and running only what lacks one. A mutation run is the exception: the head's tests can read `PATH`, `HOME` and `TMPDIR`, which no key holds. So the record carries it for the round that read it, and only the host that ran it reuses it for a run of its own. The maintainer ruled so on 2026-11-15, as [the amendment](decisions/2026-11-15-check-run-keys-lang-under-mutation.md) records. Nothing in the store is secret: a marker is proved by a value whose hash the publisher recorded before posting. So a record carries no text a tool, a provider or the head's code wrote, by [the outside-text decision](decisions/2026-11-16-shared-records-carry-no-outside-text.md). A failed check's error, a skip's reason, a note or a caveat reads as a fixed sentence, while the full text stays in the reviewing host's own store and terminal. Once a changeset's records are in the store, everything local is cache.
